title: Efficient and Joint Hyperparameter and Architecture Search for Collaborative Filtering

problem.claim: Designing collaborative filtering models through joint hyperparameter and architecture search is challenging because the search space is large and evaluation is costly.

gap.claim: Existing work generally searches architectures or hyperparameters separately, despite their intrinsic relationship.

contributions.claim: A joint hyperparameter and architecture search method for designing collaborative filtering models.
A search-space reduction procedure that screens hyperparameter choices based on an understanding of individual hyperparameters.
A two-stage search algorithm that uses subsampled datasets for initial evaluation and fine-tunes top candidates on the full dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets report better performance than hand-designed and previously searched models.
Ablation studies and case studies are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the search framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: AutoML techniques are used to design collaborative filtering models in a data-specific manner.
Prior work separates architecture search from hyperparameter search even though they are related.
Joint search is motivated but complicated by a large search space and high evaluation cost.
The framework reduces the search space and applies a two-stage search using subsampled and full datasets.
Experiments report improved performance, with ablations and case studies supporting framework effectiveness.

unknowns: The specific collaborative filtering architectures and hyperparameters are not described.
The datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, and statistical significance are not reported.
The search algorithm and hyperparameter-screening procedure are not specified in operational detail.
